notes.title: Drake Hollow launches October 1st
notes.content:
If you are a fan of [b]The Flame in the Flood[/b], check out [b]Drake Hollow[/b], the next game from the creators, and get an [i]additional[/i] 15% off for the first week!

Wishlist it right [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/739650/Drake_Hollow/]here[/url]!

Drake Hollow is a cooperative action village-building game set in The Hollow - a blighted mirror of our world - in which players protect villages of Drakes; the lovable, local vegetable folk. Either solo or with friends, players explore a dynamically generated and aether-swept world of islands to defend the Drakes from a menagerie of feral beasts, all while helping them to maintain their camps. 

Mysteries and rewards, as well as danger, await those curious enough to search every nook and cranny of The Hollow. Drakes are hungry, thirsty, and need a place to sleep. They can also - quite literally - die of boredom. Players will explore the wilderness and set up valuable supply routes to bring essentials back to camp, while keeping the Drakes entertained and happy (think yoga and puppet shows). Defending the Drakes from enemies with weapons ranging from tennis rackets to nail guns, players will eventually unravel the peculiar and ancient connection between The Hollow and our own world.

notes.title: Twitch Prime's free games for February include Downwell, Dear Esther
notes.content:
Twitch has unveiled the line-up of games that Twitch Prime members can download and keep for nowt as part of their subscription in February: Dear Esther, Downwell, The Flame in the Flood, and Draknek & Co Puzzle Collection.

It's a strong selection of titles, even if most have been around the block a few times. Enjoyable survival adventure The Flame in the Flood, for instance, has already been offered as a Twitch Prime freebie before. If you didn't snag it then, however, it's definitely worth doing so now.

Developed by The Molasses Flood and released in 2016, it delivers a wonderfully atmospheric, and distinctly soggy, twist on the well-worn rogue-lite survival formula. The general gist is that you, along with your trusty canine pal, set forth down a procedurally generated, frequently tumultuous river, stopping off at the occasional island to scavenge supplies, and craft up useful items to keep your perilous journey going just that little bit longer. Eurogamer's Christian Donlan even liked it enough to give it a Recommend badge in his review.

Read more…

notes.title: Have You Played The Flame In The Flood?
notes.content:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time…

I really really really like The Flame In The Flood. I am terrible at it, rarely reaching even the mid stage of the river, but I love it. The flood of the title is one that has swept through America, swelling the banks of a regular river until it s a wide and treacherous one. Only small islands of safety are left – an old fish bait shop, a homestead, a patch of wilderness – and they re not even always safe. Sometimes there s a big angry boar or a starving wolf.

The flame is you. And your little dog.

notes.title: New update released!
notes.content:
We’ve just released a new patch for The Flame in the Flood!

Our main goals are to fix bugs, and alleviate some frustration and quality of life issues that people have given us feedback on. 

The main changes are as follows:
[list]
[*][b]Added Director’s Commentary:[/b] the previously PS4 exclusive director’s commentary is available for all. To enable it, you can toggle it on in the options screen.
[*][b]Fixed Save Loss:[/b] We identified an issue leading to save loss when attempting to continue. If you died during a process that advanced the clock (sitting at a fire, sleeping, docking) your save would enter an unreadable state, and checkpoints would no longer work in campaign.
[*][b]Achievement fixes:[/b] We fixed a number of issues with achievements failing to register, including Paleo Diet.
[*][b]Inventory: Added “discard all” option:[/b] For stacked items, you can now discard the whole stack at once.
[*][b]Inventory: Auto-sort items into existing stacks:[/b] When you pick up an item, it will auto-sort into any existing available stacks, or the first available inventory slot if no stacks are available. For example, if you’ve got a partial stack on Aesop, a new item will auto-sort to that stack, rather than into your backpack.
[*][b]Rabbit refactor:[/b] Rabbits now behave like other animals, in that you no longer need to skin them as a crafting recipe, and killing a live captured rabbit can be done from an inventory contextual menu.
[*][b]Fire crafting can be done in proximity to a fire:[/b] Fire recipes are now available near fires, not just while sitting at them.
[*][b]Added “Craft Multiple” button:[/b] Crafts the maximum possible of an item, so you don’t need to click over and over.
[*][b]More starting bag slots on traveler:[/b] New games on traveler difficulty have 2 pouches worth of bag slots already available.
[*][b]Crafting cost changes:[/b] Arrows only require 1 feather, sumac tea can be made with 1 sumac.
[*][b]Tools can be crafted with a full inventory:[/b] You no longer need to drop something to make a knife if your bags are full. Additionally, if you craft a tool that you already have, it will replace and refresh the durability of the existing tool.
[*][b]Inventory Stacking Changes:[/b] Stack sizes increased across the board, and many previously unstackable items can now be stacked, including jars, jar items, traps, and torches.
[*][b]Added UI element for equipped torch:[/b] it indicates the life remaining.
[*][b]Added quest caches at every camp:[/b] So now you can reliably find them.
[*][b]Added “mute dog” option:[/b] Sorry Aesop, not everyone likes those barks!
[*][b]Marina spawning on endless:[/b] Marinas now spawn continuously on endless.
[/list]

If you check it out and have any issues, please let us know. You can email us at support@themolassesflood.com, message us on [url=https://www.facebook.com/molassesflood/]facebook[/url] or [url=https://twitter.com/molassesflood]twitter[/url], or leave a comment in Steam discussions.

[*][b]Added Director’s Commentary:[/b] the previously PS4 exclusive director’s commentary is available for all. To enable it, you can toggle it on in the options screen.
[*][b]Fixed Save Loss:[/b] We identified an issue leading to save loss when attempting to continue. If you died during a process that advanced the clock (sitting at a fire, sleeping, docking) your save would enter an unreadable state, and checkpoints would no longer work in campaign.
[*][b]Achievement fixes:[/b] We fixed a number of issues with achievements failing to register, including Paleo Diet.
[*][b]Inventory: Added “discard all” option:[/b] For stacked items, you can now discard the whole stack at once.
[*][b]Inventory: Auto-sort items into existing stacks:[/b] When you pick up an item, it will auto-sort into any existing available stacks, or the first available inventory slot if no stacks are available. For example, if you’ve got a partial stack on Aesop, a new item will auto-sort to that stack, rather than into your backpack.
[*][b]Rabbit refactor:[/b] Rabbits now behave like other animals, in that you no longer need to skin them as a crafting recipe, and killing a live captured rabbit can be done from an inventory contextual menu.
[*][b]Fire crafting can be done in proximity to a fire:[/b] Fire recipes are now available near fires, not just while sitting at them.
[*][b]Added “Craft Multiple” button:[/b] Crafts the maximum possible of an item, so you don’t need to click over and over.
[*][b]More starting bag slots on traveler:[/b] New games on traveler difficulty have 2 pouches worth of bag slots already available.
[*][b]Crafting cost changes:[/b] Arrows only require 1 feather, sumac tea can be made with 1 sumac.
[*][b]Tools can be crafted with a full inventory:[/b] You no longer need to drop something to make a knife if your bags are full. Additionally, if you craft a tool that you already have, it will replace and refresh the durability of the existing tool.
[*][b]Inventory Stacking Changes:[/b] Stack sizes increased across the board, and many previously unstackable items can now be stacked, including jars, jar items, traps, and torches.
[*][b]Added UI element for equipped torch:[/b] it indicates the life remaining.
[*][b]Added quest caches at every camp:[/b] So now you can reliably find them.
[*][b]Added “mute dog” option:[/b] Sorry Aesop, not everyone likes those barks!
[*][b]Marina spawning on endless:[/b] Marinas now spawn continuously on endless.
[/list]

If you check it out and have any issues, please let us know. You can email us at support@themolassesflood.com, message us on [url=https://www.facebook.com/molassesflood/]facebook[/url] or [url=https://twitter.com/molassesflood]twitter[/url], or leave a comment in Steam discussions.

notes.title: Launch date for Early Access
notes.content:
Today is an exciting day for us. We’ve pinned down a date, and are ready to tell the world.

[h1]We’re coming to Early Access on Steam on September 24th, at 10 AM PST![/h1]

For those of you who backed us on Kickstarter and have already been playing, our early access launch will also include an update with a number of new features. Along with the usual bug fixes and bits of polish, we’ll have a [b]new biome[/b], [b]raft upgrading[/b], and [b]endless mode[/b]. The new biome is the industrial area. It has fewer supplies and opportunities for shelter, so stocking up before hand will be very important. Raft upgrading includes a number of enhancements to the raft, to help overcome the lack of resources as you travel further. Upgrades include things like a stove, where you can cook food and warm yourself, and a motor, which will allow you to propel down river faster when you hit still water. Endless mode allows players to see how long they can survive.

We’re really excited (and a little nervous) about going wider, but have been reassured by the great feedback we’ve seen from backers, the press, and streamers who have had a chance to play. It’s been a crazy year for us, and is only picking up from here. It’s hard to fathom that we formed this team just over a year ago, and launched our Kickstarter less than a year ago. We’re all from AAA backgrounds, so going from idea to launch in just over a year feels like a breakneck pace for us. We’re indebted to everyone who’s played, shared us on various social media, backed the project, and taken the time to offer feedback. We couldn’t be doing this without you all.

Thanks so much, and we’ll see you on the river!

notes.title: Backer Beta v. 0.2
notes.content:
The September update is now live! 

This is our second major update since the beta launched, and features lots of new stuff.

As a reminder, if you want to join the conversation about these changes, or the game in general, come join our TFITF [url=https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/tfitf-backers]Backer Beta Google Group[/url]!

Here are the update highlights!

[b]Water V3[/b]

We’ve again tweaked the way that water works. Now rather than carrying a single canteen, the player can collect water in jars. These jars can also be used to hold tea or as the basis of a smoke bomb.

Furthermore, when collected, the water is “polluted”: it’s swimming with toxins and heavy metals and other contaminants. The only way to now make that water safe for consumption is to filter it. Water filters can be crafted out of rags and charcoal (now collectible from campfires) and are good for three uses.

Clean water can also be collected from a few new sources: ground pumps, wells and rain.

[b]Boars[/b]

We have a new AI type in the game: wild boars!

Boars will leave you alone … until you enter their territory. Then they will charge you ruthlessly until you leave. Protip: you do not want to be gored by a charging boar.

[b]Water Hazards[/b]

Every once in a while in a swollen raging river, uprooted trees, garbage and other debris will coalesce into a tangled house-sized clump and float downstream. Protip: don’t get hit by the tangled floating house-sized clumps. They will damage your raft.

[b]More art![/b]

Chad and Sinc continue to throw art into the game as fast as they can. This month Chad has spent on further fleshing out the small town biome, while Sinc works on assets for the next one.

[b]The Full List[/b]

In addition to the above, you will see lots of other tweaks and upgrades, including more UI improvements. Here’s the full list:

[list][b]Water updates:[/b]
[*]Water is now stored in jars
[*]Water can be collected from wells, the rain, standing water, or the river
[*]Contaminated Water must be filtered with a Water Filter (new item)
[*]Teas now require a Jar and Clean Water to brew, and occupy a Jar
[*]The Canteen has been removed
[b]Fire updates:[/b] 
[*]Charcoal can be gathered from a fire
[*]Lit fires can be used as a sleep location
[b]Buildings:[/b] 
[*]Buildings can all now be looted or slept in
[b]UI improvements:[/b]
[*]Numerous UI improvements for navigation and clarity
[*]Items can now be consumed and used directly from Aesop’s bag
[b]Options:[/b] 
[*]added more graphics options to improve performance on lower end hardware
[b]River Obstacles:[/b] 
[*]floating hazards now spawn in the river along with static islands.[/list]


[b]Known Issues[/b]

Lots of changes this month particularly with water, one of the main resources in the game. Due to this change as well as some others, the game has definitely become more forgiving! So you can likely expect this build to be a bit unbalanced toward the easy side. For those of you who are worried about losing the challenge, don’t worry, the balance issues will be shaken out and addressed in in the coming weeks!
